claims.text: Controlled epitaxial strain can shift the d-band center of Pt, Pd, or Ni catalyst surfaces.
Minimal surface alloying can shift the d-band center of Pt, Pd, or Ni catalyst surfaces.
A shift in the d-band center alters the electronic interaction between the metal surface and adsorbed reaction intermediates.
Changing the d-band center modulates the adsorption energies of key reaction intermediates.
A moderate d-band-center position produces adsorption strong enough for intermediates to react but weak enough for products or intermediates to desorb readily.
Optimal intermediate adsorption energies increase catalytic turnover frequency.
Optimal intermediate adsorption energies improve catalytic selectivity.
A d-band center too close to the Fermi level causes excessively strong adsorption.
A d-band center too far from the Fermi level causes excessively weak adsorption.
Excessively strong adsorption can lower catalytic activity through site poisoning.
Catalysts with an optimally shifted d-band center will have higher turnover frequency than an otherwise comparable unstrained catalyst.
Catalysts with an optimally shifted d-band center will have better selectivity than an otherwise comparable unstrained catalyst.
The proposed relationship applies to clean late-transition-metal surfaces such as Pt, Pd, or Ni under moderate conditions when morphology, particle size, and support effects are held constant.
Significant adsorbate-induced restructuring may cause deviations from the proposed d-band-center relationship.
Prior DFT and experimental studies support a correlation between d-band characteristics and catalytic performance.
The exact optimal d-band-center shift has not been precisely quantified.
The magnitude of the expected turnover-frequency improvement has not been precisely quantified.
